title: Cocoon Nebula Wide Field
explanation:
# The Cocoon Nebula: A Cosmic Imposter

Deep in the constellation Cygnus, a stellar nursery called the Cocoon Nebula tricks our eyes into seeing a comet—its bright, glowing head spans 10 light-years while a dark tail of cosmic dust stretches nearly 100 light-years behind it, all located 2,500 light-years from Earth. Within those shadowy dust filaments, baby stars are quietly forming, hidden from view but powered by a brilliant star at the nebula's center that's carving out a cavity in the surrounding cosmic clouds.
